properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 8:39PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river system will continue to bring multiple rounds
of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area, with an additional 1.5 to
2.5 inches through Thursday night. Localized higher amounts are
possible due to terrain effects. Overall the moderate to heavy
rainfall is expected to last into the overnight hours with little
break in between.

Montana Creek and Jordan Creek are expected to see minor flooding
into Friday morning after these rounds of heavy rainfall. Other
creeks and rivers in the Juneau area will still see rises through
the night into Friday morning, however no flooding is anticipated
for other streams at this time.

For more information on the minor flooding expected for Montana
Creek and Jordan Creek, please see the new Flood Advisory product at
weather.gov/juneau and stay tuned to updates as we continue to
monitor the situation.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 8:35PM AKDT until October 17 at 1:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river storm system moving into the panhandle is
expected to bring heavy rainfall Thursday night into Friday morning.
This longer duration of heavy rainfall with will allow for river and
creek rises, with minor flooding of small streams expected going into
Friday morning.

* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Areas around Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.

* WHEN...Until 130 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas, as
well as area streams and rivers. Water over roadways. Possible
isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 830 PM AKDT, satellite estimates indicate heavy rain across
the advisory area. Rapid river rises will cause minor flooding of
small streams, especially near Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.
Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of rain has fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 0.15-0.3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1.5 to 2.5 inches are possible.

- Montana Creek is anticipated to begin to fall below Minor flood
stage by late Friday morning to midday, while Jordan Creek will
stay above Minor flood stage a bit longer into the day, falling
below Minor flood stage by Friday night.

- For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 12:00pm the stage was 7.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.9 feet is expected around 1:00pm
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
8:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
10:00pm.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.

- For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.7 feet is expected around 7:00am
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
5:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
9:00am.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
At 15.5 feet: Up to one half foot of water will flow over the low
water crossing on Montana Creek Road after the community gardens.
Water will approach and begin to inundate yards of residences along
the Northwest side of Mendenhall Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

If you live near or along Montana Creek or Jordan Creek stay alert
and be prepared to take action.

properties.areaDesc: Ketchikan Gateway Borough; Annette Island
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 8:29PM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river continues to move over the panhandle
Thursday evening, lasting through Friday morning. Multiple waves
moving up will bring persistent moderate to heavy rain for much of
the southern half of the panhandle, with the heaviest rain expected
through Thursday night. Elevated gusty winds are expected alongside
this heavier rainfall, with the strongest winds expected Thursday
night. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce
significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding. Gusty winds alongside the long duration heavy rainfall will
bring a possibility of isolated landslides.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Southern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
Isolated landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Ketchikan and Metlakatla area are still expected
to be around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals favoring
southern facing mountain sides. Highest rain rates are currently
expected through this evening, where rates could exceed 0.5
inches per hour.

We will continue to see winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 55
mph at sea level, and exceeding 60 mph at elevation, with the
highest winds expected Thursday night. With the multiple rounds
of moderate to heavy rainfall and the elevated winds, there is
possibility for isolated landslides along steep mountain slopes.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible landslides.
